Posterior simulation of four-component frontier coefficients

Source: R/add_posterior_coefficients.sfmodel4.R
add_posterior_coefficients.sfmodel4_exp.Rd

Runs the Gibbs sampler on a model prepared by create_sfmodel4_exp or create_sfmodel4_hn and adds the draws to it.

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel4_exp'
add_posterior_coefficients(
  object,
  posterior_function = NULL,
  keep_u = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel4_hn'
add_posterior_coefficients(
  object,
  posterior_function = NULL,
  keep_u = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

an object of class "sfmodel4_exp" or "sfmodel4_hn".

posterior_function

the function to be applied to the model in argument object. If NULL, the package's own sampler is used.

keep_u

whether to store the draws of the unit effects and of both one-sided terms, which efficiency needs. The transient terms alone are one column per observation, so on a panel of any size this block dominates everything else: a hundred thousand observations and twenty thousand draws come to sixteen gigabytes. A positive whole number stores every that-many-th retained draw instead, which divides the storage by it and cannot exceed the number of retained draws. A warning is issued before anything is allocated if the block would exceed a gigabyte.

verbose

either FALSE, TRUE for progress at every ten per cent of iterations, or an integer reporting interval.

...

further arguments passed to or from other methods.

Value

The object in object with the element posterior added. Alongside beta and sigma_v it holds sigma_mu, the two inefficiency parameters under the names the model gives them, and, if keep_u is TRUE, the draws of the unit effects mu, the persistent terms eta and the transient terms u.

Details

Each sweep draws the transient inefficiency terms, the persistent inefficiency terms and the unit effects from their full conditionals, then the coefficients and the variance parameters. Every one of those conditionals is standard: the one-sided terms are truncated normals, the unit effects are normal, and the variances are gamma. Adding two components to the sampler of add_posterior_coefficients therefore changes the loop but not the algorithm.

Convergence deserves more attention here than in the two-component models. The unit effect and persistent inefficiency are both constant within a unit and are separated only by the sign restriction, so the two can trade off against each other from sweep to sweep and mix slowly. Run several chains from add_initial_values(method = "prior") and look at sigma_mu alongside the persistent inefficiency parameter before trusting the split.

See also

efficiency for the three efficiency concepts the model distinguishes.

Other posterior simulation: add_posterior_coefficients(), add_posterior_loglik.sfmodel4()

Examples

set.seed(1234)
d <- sim_sf4(n = 60, n_time = 8, beta = c(1, 0.5, 0.3))

model <- create_sfmodel4_exp(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d, id = "id",
                             iterations = 500, burnin = 200)
model <- add_posterior_coefficients(add_priors(model))

summary(model)
